_comment: World bible sections 7 and 13, cut into the pieces the Lore tab reads. `seas` is one Sea's character, taken from the italic line under its heading in docs/lore.md. `archetypes` is what kind of place an island is — ten of them cover seventy-one islands, which is the same trick the paintings use, and it means every island has something true to say about itself and not only the eleven the bible names. Written to be read in the island's own panel, so no sentence here refers to the war.

seas.The Crown Sea: Inner water, temperate and grey, and fortified to the last rock. The names here are stately because the Imperium gave them, and the seawalls are older than the Imperium.
seas.The Merchant Sea: Inner water, and the busiest of the seven. Whale oil, timber and rope go out of it in every direction, and the charts are worn through where the routes cross.
seas.The Bone Sea: Inner water over a shoal graveyard. Every chart of it is a chart of what has already been lost here, and the wreckers ashore make a living from the next one.
seas.The Far Sea: Outer water, and cold enough that the rigging ices in the night. Ice islands, whaling stations, and the long dark in winter.
seas.The Sea of Storms: Outer water in the monsoon belt: typhoons off the deep, volcanoes ashore, rice terraces and jungle between. Rich ground and hard to keep hold of.
seas.The Glass Sea: Outer water, flat and blinding, over salt flats and drowned temple ground. Sound carries strangely here and the horizon is never quite where it should be.
seas.The Amber Sea: Outer water, warm and shallow, turquoise over reef. Stilt villages, signal towers, and lagoons that a deep hull cannot enter at all.

archetypes.jungle-isle: Green to the waterline, and the green closes over anything that stops being cut back. What grows here grows faster than it can be carried away, which makes the island rich and makes holding it work.
archetypes.rock-isle: Bare stone out of deep water, with a landing on the one side that has a beach. Nothing grows and nothing hides; what the island is worth is where it sits.
archetypes.port-city: A working harbour with a town behind it — quays, warehouses, a customs house, and more people than the island could feed on its own. Ships are the whole of why it exists.
archetypes.free-harbor: No governor, no customs, and no questions at the quay. A harbour like this keeps itself by being useful to everybody and belonging to nobody.
archetypes.mining-isle: Cut open for what is under it. Spoil heaps, a tramway down to the water, and a troop of men who came for the work and stayed because there was nowhere else to go.
archetypes.reef-isle: Low ground inside a reef, where the water is clear enough to see the bottom and shallow enough to take the bottom out of a careless hull. The channel in is local knowledge.
archetypes.storm-isle: Weather comes off the deep here with nothing to break it. Roofs are lashed, boats are hauled well up, and half the year is spent waiting for the other half.
archetypes.ice-isle: Rock and ice, and a sea that freezes at the edges. Whale oil and sealskin go out; everything else comes in, and in winter nothing comes in at all.
archetypes.drowned-isle: Old stonework standing in the shallows — steps, columns, a doorway to nothing — from whoever was here before the water rose. The living town sits above the tide line and does not talk about the rest.
archetypes.tide-isle: The sea takes half of it twice a day and gives it back. Causeways that are roads at noon and channels by evening, and a people who plan their whole day around the water.
